result.question: Do universal MLIPs preserve the chemical decision (which of two near-degenerate conformers is lower) even when their energy MAE is tiny?
result.data: SPICE 1.1.4, 16089 decision pairs from 1588 molecules, sub-1 kcal/mol, 404 charged molecules with SMILES-parsed charge/spin
result.headline: Energy error does not predict decision quality: the classical baseline has 206x the best model's error yet still orders 56% correctly, and the best model still reverses 10% of near-degenerate pairs.

verification: Every published row recomputes exactly from its committed decisions CSV (decision_scores).
ORB raw covers 15232/15232 conformers, 0 missing, 0 NaN.
44 tests pass, including tests/test_readme_claims.py which parses the README table cells.
GitHub Actions green on the final commit.
Six figures each passed a vision QA pass; every defect it found was fixed at the cause.
defects_found_and_fixed: SPICE conformations are BOHR; treated as Angstrom gave chance-level accuracy (0.489 -> 0.747 once fixed).
SPICE layout guessed wrong (stacked conformations, not per-conformer groups).
Charged molecules were silently run neutral; now SMILES-parsed with an RDKit-free fallback.
Round-to-6dp flipped the sign of 28 near-zero MMFF gaps, making CSV and summary disagree.
A stale 1500-conformer ORB artefact produced a published 0.893 that did not reproduce; withdrawn, re-run, re-published as 0.900.
Overlapping chunk ranges double-counted 2400 conformers; merge now dedupes by id.
Licences were guessed wrong (ORB is Apache-2.0, not ASL; MACE is MIT code + ASL weights).
next_action: none. Optional future work is listed in the README limits (CCSD(T) reference, reaction energies instead of conformer pairs, per-assay clustered CIs).
